title: Start neutral, then tilt the book long/short (x1.5/x0.5 or skip the against-trend side) from an early-session direction call (QQQ from-open 0.25/0.50%, breadth 0.60/0.40, SPY+QQQ+breadth agreement) at 10:00/10:15/10:30/11:00 or re-evaluated through 13:00
hypothesis: The early-session move tells which side of the book to favour for the rest of the day.
result: 0/76 pass (bar 2.94; lineage 3.96). Primary book (12 setups, 97% short, valid parent -0.040R/trade). Pure direction tilt (M1 x1.5/x0.5): best valid delta +0.001R (fade Q50@10:30), every non-fade M1 valid delta <= 0 on Primary. Skip-against (M2): best valid S-Q50-1030-M2 +0.011R t 2.27, S-Q25-1015-M2 +0.015R t 2.11, but excess vs a random tilt with the same switching frequency is negative (-0.001 / -0.004R) and delta is negative in down sessions: it only trims exposure to a negative book. Pooled P+T1 best direction info S-Q25-1000-M1 valid +0.006R t 0.94 (train +0.0045 t 0.57). Hindsight ceiling (true session direction from 10:00, M1): +0.033R valid t 5.4, so the setups do care about direction; the early call does not deliver it (Part A: rest-of-day hit 49-52% valid vs 51-52% always-long).

title: Use the index gap state at 10:30-11:00 (gap unfilled = continue gap direction, gap filled = fade it) as the direction input for a long/short tilt
hypothesis: Of 13 early features, gap state is the only one whose rest-of-day / afternoon association has the same sign on train and valid for SPY, QQQ and IWM (Spearman positive in all 48 index x checkpoint x target x split cells, +0.005..+0.165, mean about +0.06; hit 53-55%), though no cell clears the Part A bar (|t| >= 3.39). Untested as a tilt; it would add configurations to the market-context-gate lineage (bar ~3.96), so expect a small effect and a likely fail; low priority.
